answer: The dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices ensure Sybil resistance by compelling each identity's pigment of value to be directly linked to its unique contributions; thus, multiplying identities diminishes expected payoff, analogous to scattering pigment over a wide area, diluting its intensity. In adversarial environments, adversaries harbor no advantage as Nash equilibrium converges, paralleling a mirror reflecting light equally from all sides, discouraging any attempt to multiply or distort value.
